title: Applicability, Jurisdiction and Material Perimeter
objective: Establish the material and territorial boundaries of digital personal data processing within and outside India.
legal_reference_summary: The Act applies to the processing of digital personal data within India, and outside India if in connection with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India. Excludes personal/domestic use and publicly available data.
applicability_conditions: Applies universally to any entity processing personal data in digital form.
assessment_question: Has the organisation documented its digital personal data inventory, established jurisdictional boundaries, and identified all digital collection touchpoints?
implementation_expectations: Maintain an exhaustive inventory of digital processing activities (RoPA), categorising personal data collected within India or from Indian Data Principals abroad.
evidence_limitations: Verbal assertions without a documented data inventory are insufficient.
assessment_guidance: Verify whether offline data digitised subsequently is brought into scope as mandated by Section 3(a)(ii).
risk_guidance: Operating outside defined compliance scope risks unmonitored regulatory exposure across all processing streams.
suggested_remediation: Implement an enterprise Data Processing Activities Registry (RoPA) cataloguing data flows, storage locations, and legal entities.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Lawful Basis and Ground of Processing
objective: Ensure all personal data processing is underpinned by valid consent or an exhaustive statutory legitimate use.
legal_reference_summary: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given consent (Section 6), or for certain legitimate uses specified under Section 7.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all processing activities across all business units.
applicability_rationale: Foundational rule; no processing can exist without a valid statutory ground.
assessment_question: Is every personal data processing activity formally mapped to a distinct statutory ground (valid consent under Section 6 or an exhaustive legitimate use under Section 7)?
implementation_expectations: Document the legal ground for every data processing activity in the RoPA; eliminate processing lacking a valid statutory anchor.
evidence_limitations: High-level privacy policies without activity-level legal mapping do not demonstrate compliance.
assessment_guidance: Confirm that the organisation does not rely on generic 'business interest' claims outside the exhaustive list of Section 7.
risk_guidance: Processing without a lawful basis constitutes an unlawful act under Section 4, exposing the fiduciary to statutory scrutiny.
suggested_remediation: Conduct a legal grounds audit mapping each personal data collection workflow to either Section 6 (Consent) or a Section 7 clause.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Itemised and Pre-Consent Notice
objective: Provide Data Principals with clear, itemised notice before seeking consent.
legal_reference_summary: Notice must be given before or at the time of seeking consent. It must specify the personal data sought, the specific itemised purpose, the manner of exercising Section 11 rights, and the manner of making complaints to the DPBI.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all activities where personal data is collected on the basis of consent.
assessment_question: Does the organisation provide a clear, standalone, itemised notice before or at the time of requesting consent, detailing data types, purpose, rights, and DPBI complaint procedures?
implementation_expectations: Deploy discrete pre-consent notices detailing data fields, specific itemised purposes, DSAR instructions, and grievance redressal steps.
evidence_limitations: Generic website terms of service or privacy policies bundled with commercial conditions do not satisfy Section 5(1).
assessment_guidance: Inspect actual collection touchpoints to verify notice timing and content.
risk_guidance: Inadequate or bundled notice invalidates consent under Section 6(1), undermining the legality of processing.
suggested_remediation: Redesign onboarding UI/UX to display standalone, itemised notices prior to consent checkboxes.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Historical Notice for Pre-Existing Consent
objective: Inform existing Data Principals of processing details for legacy consent captured prior to commencement.
legal_reference_summary: Where consent was collected prior to commencement, notice informing the Data Principal of data, purpose, rights, and DPBI grievance route must be dispatched as soon as practicable.
applicability_conditions: Applies to fiduciaries holding legacy personal data collected prior to 13 May 2027.
applicability_rationale: Mandatory for entities with legacy customer/user databases.
assessment_question: Has the organisation planned or dispatched retrospective notices to existing Data Principals whose consent was captured prior to the commencement of the Act?
implementation_expectations: Implement a communication protocol to send compliant Section 5 notices to existing registered users upon commencement.
evidence_limitations: Marketing email campaigns without statutory notice elements do not qualify.
assessment_guidance: Verify communications schedules, customer notification email/SMS templates, and audit logs.
risk_guidance: Continuing processing legacy data without issuing statutory notice exposes the fiduciary to non-compliance penalties.
suggested_remediation: Draft and schedule a grandfathering notice communication plan for all active registered users.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Multilingual Notice Option Mechanism
objective: Enable Data Principals to access notices in English or any Eighth Schedule language.
legal_reference_summary: The Data Principal shall be given an option to access the contents of the notice in English or any of the 22 languages specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all consumer-facing and public-facing Data Fiduciaries seeking consent.
assessment_question: Does the organisation provide an operational mechanism (e.g. language toggle or accessible translated views) allowing Data Principals to view notices in English or any Eighth Schedule language?
implementation_expectations: Implement UI language selection toggles or certified translated versions of the privacy notice across 22 Eighth Schedule languages.
evidence_limitations: Stating that a translation tool can be used by the user in their browser does not satisfy the statutory mandate under Section 5(3).
assessment_guidance: Verify that certified translations or verified dynamic localization engines are integrated into the customer onboarding path.
risk_guidance: Failure to provide Eighth Schedule multilingual options constitutes a breach of notice obligations under Section 5.
suggested_remediation: Commission certified translations of statutory notices and implement an accessible language selector on public portals.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-01; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Unbundled Affirmative Consent Architecture
objective: Capture affirmative, unbundled, and unambiguous consent free from dark patterns.
legal_reference_summary: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, and signified by clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes, bundled terms, or forced consent for non-essential purposes are prohibited.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all processing activities relying on consent.
applicability_rationale: Mandatory statutory provision for consent-based processing.
assessment_question: Are consent mechanisms unbundled, free from dark patterns and pre-ticked checkboxes, and captured through clear affirmative action with cryptographic timestamps?
implementation_expectations: Configure consent collection with unchecked boxes, separate consent toggles for distinct purposes, and an immutable consent logging system.
evidence_limitations: Merely showing a 'By clicking Submit you agree to our Terms' button fails the unconditional and affirmative action test.
assessment_guidance: Inspect live registration flows across web, mobile, and offline channels.
risk_guidance: Invalid or bundled consent nullifies the legal basis of processing under Section 6.
suggested_remediation: Remove pre-ticked checkboxes and decouple service delivery from optional data collection.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Consent Withdrawal Mechanism and Comparable Ease
objective: Enable Data Principals to withdraw consent with ease comparable to giving it.
legal_reference_summary: Data Principals have the right to withdraw consent at any time. Ease of withdrawal must be comparable to ease of granting. Upon withdrawal, fiduciary must cease processing within reasonable time.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all consent-based processing systems.
assessment_question: Does the organisation provide an accessible, frictionless mechanism allowing Data Principals to withdraw consent with ease comparable to granting it, triggering automated cessation of processing?
implementation_expectations: Deploy self-service consent management preference centers (e.g. 1-click opt-out) integrated with backend data pipelines.
evidence_limitations: Requiring physical letters or complex manual customer service calls to withdraw digitally given consent violates Section 6(4).
assessment_guidance: Compare the steps required to give consent vs the steps required to withdraw.
risk_guidance: Obstructing consent withdrawal violates Section 6(4) and triggers mandatory erasure requirements under Section 8(7).
suggested_remediation: Build a self-service privacy preference center in mobile apps and web account settings.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Consent Manager Interoperability
objective: Support electronic consent giving, management, and withdrawal through registered Consent Managers.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Principal may give, manage, review, or withdraw consent through a registered Consent Manager. Consent Managers must be registered with DPBI and satisfy Rule 4 standards.
applicability_conditions: Applies to organisations interfacing with or acting as registered Consent Managers.
assessment_question: Is the organisation equipped with technical APIs and interoperability workflows to receive, verify, and execute consent instructions from registered Consent Managers?
implementation_expectations: Integrate standard API endpoints to ingest and validate consent artifacts dispatched by registered Consent Managers.
evidence_limitations: Architecture drafts without implemented API specifications are insufficient.
assessment_guidance: Verify whether system architecture accommodates external consent lifecycle webhooks.
risk_guidance: Inability to honor Consent Manager requests once operational creates regulatory non-compliance under Section 6(9).
suggested_remediation: Design an inbound Consent Artifact ingestion gateway supporting MeitY/DPBI electronic data interchange standards.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-02; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Voluntary Provision Legitimate Uses
objective: Confine processing under voluntary provision strictly to specified purposes.
legal_reference_summary: Processing without explicit consent is lawful where the Data Principal voluntarily provides personal data for a specified purpose and has not indicated withholding of consent.
applicability_conditions: Applies to workflows relying on voluntary provision (e.g. inbound queries).
assessment_question: Where processing relies on voluntary provision under Section 7(a), is processing strictly confined to the specific purpose for which the data was provided?
implementation_expectations: Document controls ensuring data voluntarily furnished for one purpose (e.g., support ticket) is not repurposed for marketing.
evidence_limitations: Repurposing voluntary support data for unsolicited sales outreach violates Section 7(a).
assessment_guidance: Verify whether data boundaries and access restrictions prevent secondary processing.
risk_guidance: Exceeding the scope of voluntary provision constitutes unlawful processing under Section 4.
suggested_remediation: Establish technical partition tags preventing voluntary customer enquiry data from synchronizing to marketing databases.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Employment Functions Legitimate Uses
objective: Process employee data strictly within legitimate employment purposes without disproportionate surveillance.
legal_reference_summary: Personal data may be processed without consent for the purposes of employment or for safeguarding the employer from loss or liability.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all employers processing employee data.
applicability_rationale: Legitimate use exception for HR/workplace data.
assessment_question: Does the organisation process employee personal data strictly within the boundaries of employment functions, benefits administration, and asset protection without excessive surveillance?
implementation_expectations: Maintain an Employee Privacy Notice and HR Processing Policy defining permissible monitoring and data handling boundaries.
evidence_limitations: Invasive personal device monitoring without employment nexus cannot be justified under Section 7(g).
assessment_guidance: Inspect employee handbooks, monitoring disclosures, and BYOD policies.
risk_guidance: Unjustified surveillance beyond Section 7(g) boundaries violates statutory grounds.
suggested_remediation: Formalise an Employee Data Protection SOP clarifying legitimate employment use cases and data retention limits.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-03; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Accountability and Non-Delegable Responsibility
objective: Maintain non-delegable responsibility for compliance across internal operations and processors.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary shall be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all Data Fiduciaries.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain enterprise-wide governance, policies, and audit mechanisms ensuring accountability for all processing conducted internally and through external vendors?
implementation_expectations: Formulate board-approved data protection governance charters, appoint privacy leads, and conduct regular internal compliance reviews.
evidence_limitations: Shifting full compliance responsibility onto cloud providers or IT vendors is legally void under Section 8(1).
assessment_guidance: Review executive accountability reporting, compliance charters, and vendor oversight mechanisms.
risk_guidance: Fiduciary remains solely liable before the DPBI for statutory violations committed by downstream processors.
suggested_remediation: Establish a Data Protection Committee and implement formal third-party risk governance.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Data Processor Engagement and Contractual Governance
objective: Bind all third-party Data Processors under valid contracts containing mandatory statutory clauses.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary may engage, appoint, use or otherwise involve a Data Processor only under a valid contract. Rule 7 specifies mandatory clauses: processing scope, confidentiality, technical security, breach notice, sub-processor restrictions, and audit rights.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all fiduciaries engaging third-party software, cloud hosts, or outsourcing agencies.
assessment_question: Are all third-party Data Processors bound by legally executed Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) incorporating mandatory Rule 7 clauses?
implementation_expectations: Execute standardized DPAs with all cloud hosts, SaaS providers, and service vendors processing personal data.
evidence_limitations: Standard commercial purchase orders without privacy and security schedules fail Section 8(2).
assessment_guidance: Review a sample of executed vendor contracts across cloud infrastructure, HR SaaS, and customer support vendors.
risk_guidance: Engaging an uncontracted processor violates Section 8(2) and exposes fiduciary to direct liability for vendor breaches.
suggested_remediation: Establish an enterprise DPA remediation workflow to execute supplemental data protection terms with all active vendors.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-04; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Data Quality, Accuracy and Decision Safeguards
objective: Ensure personal data completeness, accuracy, and consistency when used for decision-making or disclosure.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary shall ensure data completeness, accuracy, and consistency if personal data is used to make a decision that affects the Data Principal, or is disclosed to another Data Fiduciary.
applicability_conditions: Applies to fiduciaries using personal data for automated scoring, underwriting, reviews, or external sharing.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain data validation, deduplication, and quality controls to guarantee accuracy when personal data affects Data Principals or is disclosed to third parties?
implementation_expectations: Implement database input validation routines, deduplication engines, and self-service correction mechanisms.
evidence_limitations: Manual ad-hoc corrections without documented quality validation protocols do not satisfy Section 8(3).
assessment_guidance: Test data validation rules on onboarding inputs and data exchange interfaces.
risk_guidance: Incorrect decisions resulting from inaccurate data breach Section 8(3) and provoke Data Principal claims.
suggested_remediation: Implement automated data hygiene and verification pipelines at points of collection and transformation.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Technical and Organisational Security Safeguards (TOMs)
objective: Implement reasonable technical and organisational security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure compliance, and protect personal data by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach. Maximum penalty: ₹250 Crores.
applicability_conditions: Applies universally across all systems holding digital personal data.
applicability_rationale: Top-tier statutory mandate carrying maximum penal exposure.
assessment_question: Has the organisation implemented verified technical and organisational security measures (access controls, vulnerability assessments, network segmentation, multi-factor authentication) to prevent data breaches?
implementation_expectations: Deploy ISO 27001 / SOC 2 aligned security baselines: annual VAPT, strict MFA on employee portals, role-based database access, and patch management.
evidence_limitations: Stale VAPT reports older than 12 months or unresolved critical vulnerabilities invalidate claims of reasonable safeguards.
assessment_guidance: Inspect recent penetration test executive summaries and remediation verification letters.
risk_guidance: Absence of reasonable safeguards exposes organisation to maximum statutory penalty under Schedule Tier 1 (up to ₹250 Crores).
suggested_remediation: Commission an immediate external VAPT audit and remediate all high/critical vulnerabilities on personal data repositories.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Encryption, Key Governance and Access Controls
objective: Enforce strong encryption at rest and in transit with secure key management.
legal_reference_summary: Reasonable safeguards require protecting data in transit and at rest using standard cryptographic mechanisms, key isolation, and least-privilege identity access management.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all databases, object stores, and transmission channels carrying personal data.
assessment_question: Is all digital personal data encrypted at rest (e.g. AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+ / 1.3), supported by secure KMS key rotation and least-privilege access?
implementation_expectations: Enforce TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, automated annual key rotation via KMS/HSM, and zero plaintext personal data storage.
evidence_limitations: Hardcoded encryption keys in source repositories or plaintext database backups fail Section 8(5).
assessment_guidance: Inspect database configuration snapshots and TLS ciphersuite audit reports.
risk_guidance: Plaintext data exfiltration turns an intrusion into a catastrophic data breach with maximum liability.
suggested_remediation: Enable automated KMS encryption at rest across all cloud storage buckets and relational database volumes.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Personal Data Breach Incident Response and Triage
objective: Maintain operational incident response playbooks for detecting, containing, and triaging personal data breaches.
legal_reference_summary: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall intimate the Board and each affected Data Principal. Requires documented incident management and triage SOPs. Maximum penalty: ₹200 Crores.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all Data Fiduciaries.
applicability_rationale: Mandatory statutory duty carrying Tier 2 penalty exposure.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain an operational Personal Data Breach Incident Response Plan detailing detection, escalation, containment, and root-cause analysis?
implementation_expectations: Establish a 24/7 CSIRT team, breach triage matrix, and documented escalation protocols.
evidence_limitations: Generic IT disaster recovery plans that omit personal data compromise and privacy impacts are insufficient.
assessment_guidance: Review table-top drill records and incident response playbooks.
risk_guidance: Failure to promptly detect and triage a breach leads to statutory reporting failure under Section 8(6).
suggested_remediation: Author and execute a dedicated Data Breach Incident Response Plan with annual tabletop simulation drills.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-05; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Dual Breach Intimation (DPBI and Affected Principals)
objective: Maintain capability to intimate personal data breaches to the DPBI and affected Data Principals in prescribed form.
legal_reference_summary: Mandatory intimation of personal data breach to the DPBI and to each affected Data Principal in prescribed form, manner, and timelines. Maximum penalty: ₹200 Crores.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all Data Fiduciaries.
assessment_question: Are communication templates, secure channels, and procedural workflows established to execute mandatory breach intimations to both the DPBI and affected Data Principals?
implementation_expectations: Pre-draft bilingual breach notification templates and maintain technical bulk notification channels to alert affected Data Principals without delay.
evidence_limitations: Notifying only the Board while concealing the incident from affected Data Principals violates Section 8(6).
assessment_guidance: Inspect pre-drafted communication templates for required statutory fields.
risk_guidance: Failure to intimate breach to Board or Data Principals triggers statutory penalties up to ₹200 Crores.
suggested_remediation: Configure automated communication playbooks ready to dispatch breach notices to DPBI digital portal and Data Principals.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-05; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Purpose Fulfillment and Automated Erasure
objective: Erase personal data upon consent withdrawal or purpose fulfillment unless required by law.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary must erase personal data upon consent withdrawal or as soon as purpose fulfillment occurs, unless retention is required by law.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all systems holding digital personal data.
applicability_rationale: Mandatory statutory duty enforcing storage limitation.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain defined retention schedules with automated or verified data purging when the specified purpose expires or consent is withdrawn?
implementation_expectations: Maintain a Data Retention Schedule and execute automated cron jobs / database TTL policies to purge expired personal data.
evidence_limitations: Indefinite data retention policies or failure to purge test/staging databases violate Section 8(7).
assessment_guidance: Verify database archival routines and data destruction certificates.
risk_guidance: Retaining data beyond purpose fulfillment breaches Section 8(7) and amplifies breach impact surface.
suggested_remediation: Deploy automated data lifecycle management (DLM) policies across databases and object storage.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Statutory Retention Exceptions Register
objective: Document and substantiate statutory provisions mandating retention beyond purpose fulfillment.
legal_reference_summary: Retention beyond purpose fulfillment is lawful only where explicitly required under applicable laws (e.g. Income Tax Act, PMLA, Companies Act).
applicability_conditions: Applies to all fiduciaries retaining personal data under statutory mandates.
assessment_question: Has the organisation compiled a Legal Retention Register documenting the specific statutory provisions requiring extended retention of records?
implementation_expectations: Maintain a legal citation register linking personal data categories to specific Indian statutory retention mandates.
evidence_limitations: Vague assertions of 'regulatory compliance' without citing the applicable Indian Act and section fail this control.
assessment_guidance: Review legal citations against tax, banking, corporate, and labor legislation.
risk_guidance: Unsubstantiated retention masquerading as legal obligation violates Section 8(7).
suggested_remediation: Partner with legal counsel to formulate a comprehensive statutory retention schedule mapping data types to specific enactments.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Data Principal Rights: Access and Information Summary
objective: Fulfill Data Principal requests for personal data summaries and sharing partner identities.
legal_reference_summary: The Data Principal has the right to obtain: (a) summary of personal data being processed, (b) identities of all other Data Fiduciaries and Processors with whom shared, and (c) other prescribed information.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all Data Fiduciaries processing personal data.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain a secure portal and workflow to provide Data Principals with a comprehensive summary of their processed personal data and a list of sharing partners?
implementation_expectations: Deploy a self-service DSAR access portal or request intake workflow capable of compiling personal data summaries within statutory timelines.
evidence_limitations: Requiring Data Principals to visit physical offices or pay excessive fees violates Section 11.
assessment_guidance: Test the DSAR intake form and inspect sample response summaries.
risk_guidance: Denying or ignoring valid access requests triggers Data Principal complaints to the DPBI.
suggested_remediation: Implement an automated DSAR orchestration tool linked to backend user databases.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Data Principal Rights: Correction, Update and Erasure
objective: Enable Data Principals to correct inaccurate data, complete incomplete data, and request erasure.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Principal has the right to correction of inaccurate data, completion of incomplete data, updating, and erasure of data no longer necessary for purpose or upon consent withdrawal.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all Data Fiduciaries.
assessment_question: Are procedures and self-service features in place allowing Data Principals to correct, update, complete, or request erasure of their personal data?
implementation_expectations: Provide profile editing features and a verified DSAR workflow to execute corrections and erasures across primary and replica databases.
evidence_limitations: Refusing erasure requests without citing a valid statutory retention exception violates Section 12(3).
assessment_guidance: Audit the end-to-end workflow from customer request to downstream database modification.
risk_guidance: Failure to process correction or erasure requests exposes the fiduciary to regulatory orders.
suggested_remediation: Build profile self-service editing workflows and establish technical propagation of erasures to Data Processors.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Officer Publication
objective: Publish Grievance Officer details and maintain an SLA-tracked grievance redressal mechanism.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary must establish an effective grievance redressal mechanism and publish contact details of DPO or Grievance Officer. Must resolve complaints within prescribed SLA.
applicability_conditions: Applies universally to all Data Fiduciaries.
assessment_question: Has the organisation published the contact details of an authorized Grievance Officer and established an SLA-tracked grievance redressal ticketing system?
implementation_expectations: Publish the Grievance Officer's name, email, and physical address prominently on websites/apps; maintain a ticketing SLA enforcing resolution within statutory limits.
evidence_limitations: Generic 'support@company.com' addresses without a designated human officer violate Section 8(8).
assessment_guidance: Check public privacy notice footer and test grievance ticket routing.
risk_guidance: Failure to provide grievance redressal allows Data Principals to escalate directly to the DPBI.
suggested_remediation: Formally designate an India-based Grievance Officer and configure a privacy grievance queue in the ticketing system.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Data Principal Right to Nominate
objective: Enable Data Principals to nominate a representative to exercise rights upon death or incapacity.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Principal shall have the right to nominate any other individual to exercise rights in the event of death or incapacity.
applicability_conditions: Applies to user-account and consumer-facing platforms.
assessment_question: Does the organisation provide an account feature or mechanism allowing Data Principals to nominate an individual to manage their personal data in the event of death or incapacity?
implementation_expectations: Introduce a digital nomination feature within account settings allowing users to designate a nominee with contact details.
evidence_limitations: Lacking a nomination mechanism in consumer user accounts breaches Section 14.
assessment_guidance: Verify account management screens and deceased account policy documentation.
risk_guidance: Inability to honor lawful nominee claims violates Section 14.
suggested_remediation: Add a 'Digital Nominee Designation' section to user account profile settings.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Verifiable Parental Consent for Children and Disabled
objective: Obtain verifiable parental or guardian consent before processing personal data of children or disabled persons.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary shall, before processing any personal data of a child (< 18 years) or a person with a disability, obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian. Maximum penalty: ₹200 Crores.
applicability_conditions: Applies to any organisation processing personal data of individuals under 18 years of age or persons with disabilities.
applicability_rationale: Conditional requirement; excludable only if factual proof confirms zero minor data.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain an operational age-gating mechanism and a verifiable parental/guardian consent verification process before processing children's personal data?
implementation_expectations: Deploy neutral age-screens and integrate government-approved parental verification mechanisms (e.g., DigiLocker tokenization, parental OTP verification).
evidence_limitations: Self-declaration checkboxes ('I am 18 or older') without verification are insufficient for platforms accessible to minors.
assessment_guidance: Review user onboarding flow and parental consent verification logs.
risk_guidance: Processing child data without verifiable parental consent carries statutory penalties up to ₹200 Crores.
suggested_remediation: Implement a robust age-assurance mechanism and establish a multi-step parental verification workflow.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-06; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Prohibition on Child Tracking, Profiling and Targeted Ads
objective: Enforce technical prohibitions on tracking, behavioural monitoring, and targeted advertising directed at children.
legal_reference_summary: A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children, nor undertake processing detrimental to child well-being. Maximum penalty: ₹200 Crores.
applicability_conditions: Applies to entities whose digital platforms or apps are accessed by minors.
assessment_question: Are technical controls enforced to completely disable tracking scripts, behavioural analytics, user profiling, and targeted advertising whenever an account belongs to a minor?
implementation_expectations: Configure advertising SDKs and analytics pipelines to suppress tracking cookies, user profiling, and targeted ad servers for registered minors.
evidence_limitations: Serving targeted ads to accounts flagged as minors constitutes an immediate violation of Section 9(3).
assessment_guidance: Audit network traffic and tracking SDK initialisation code for minor user profiles.
risk_guidance: Direct violation of Section 9(3) subject to Tier 2 statutory penalty (up to ₹200 Crores).
suggested_remediation: Hardcode a platform-wide privacy switch that disables all advertising identifiers and behavioral pixels for minor user IDs.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.

title: Significant Data Fiduciary Governance (Resident DPO)
objective: Appoint an India-resident Data Protection Officer reporting directly to the Board.
legal_reference_summary: Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint an India-based Data Protection Officer (DPO) who represents the fiduciary and reports directly to the Board of Directors or governing body.
applicability_conditions: Mandatory for notified Significant Data Fiduciaries; advisory for prospective candidates.
applicability_rationale: Conditional on SDF designation or prospective candidacy.
assessment_question: Has the organisation formally appointed an India-resident Data Protection Officer with independent reporting lines directly to the Board of Directors?
implementation_expectations: Issue formal board resolution appointing an India-resident DPO with direct reporting to the Board, adequate resources, and independence.
evidence_limitations: Designating a non-resident executive or subordinating the DPO to IT/marketing departments violates Section 10(2)(a).
assessment_guidance: Inspect board minutes, employment contract, and organizational reporting hierarchy.
risk_guidance: Operating as an SDF without a resident DPO breaches Section 10 obligations.
suggested_remediation: Formalise the DPO role charter and ensure the designated individual is resident in India and reports to executive governance.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-08; pending legal counsel verification.

title: SDF Impact Assessments (DPIA) and Independent Audits
objective: Conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and engage independent Data Auditors.
legal_reference_summary: An SDF must appoint an independent Data Auditor to carry out data audits, and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA).
applicability_conditions: Mandatory for notified Significant Data Fiduciaries.
assessment_question: Does the organisation conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for high-risk processing activities and engage an independent Data Auditor for annual compliance audits?
implementation_expectations: Formulate an enterprise DPIA framework and execute formal engagement contracts with external independent privacy auditors.
evidence_limitations: Internal self-assessments cannot substitute for an independent data audit under Section 10(2)(b).
assessment_guidance: Review DPIA documentation for high-risk deployments and external auditor findings.
risk_guidance: Failure to conduct DPIAs or independent audits constitutes a material SDF violation under Section 10.
suggested_remediation: Adopt an institutional DPIA methodology and establish a procurement schedule for independent annual data audits.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-08; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Cross-Border Data Transfers and Negative List
objective: Enforce controls ensuring personal data is not transferred to blacklisted countries or territories.
legal_reference_summary: The Central Government may restrict transfer of personal data outside India to notified countries/territories (negative list). Fiduciaries must not transfer personal data to blacklisted destinations.
applicability_conditions: Applies to all organisations transferring digital personal data outside India.
assessment_question: Does the organisation maintain an inventory of all cross-border data flows and enforce controls ensuring personal data is not transferred to blacklisted countries?
implementation_expectations: Maintain a Cross-Border Data Transfer Register documenting destination countries, recipient entities, and technical safeguard mechanisms.
evidence_limitations: Unmonitored overseas SaaS usage where data destination is unknown violates Section 16.
assessment_guidance: Audit network gateways, cloud region configurations, and offshore vendor contracts.
risk_guidance: Unauthorised cross-border transfers to restricted jurisdictions breach Section 16 and trigger statutory sanctions.
suggested_remediation: Implement technical cloud policies restricting data center provisioning to approved jurisdictions and document all outbound data flows.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-09; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Sectoral Data Localization Preservation
objective: Comply with higher sectoral data localization mandates preserved under Section 16(2).
legal_reference_summary: Nothing in Section 16(1) shall restrict the applicability of any law providing for a higher degree of protection or restriction on transfer (e.g. RBI payment data localization).
applicability_conditions: Applies to regulated entities (banks, NBFCs, payment aggregators, insurance providers).
assessment_question: Does the organisation comply with higher sectoral data localization mandates (such as RBI directives requiring payment data to be stored exclusively in India)?
implementation_expectations: Configure financial database clusters and primary transaction processing exclusively within sovereign Indian data centers.
evidence_limitations: Storing payment system logs exclusively in overseas cloud regions violates RBI directives preserved under Section 16(2).
assessment_guidance: Review System Audit Reports (SAR) submitted to sectoral regulators (RBI, IRDAI, SEBI).
risk_guidance: Sectoral localization violations trigger regulatory license suspension alongside DPDPA exposure.
suggested_remediation: Ensure all payment transaction data and related audit trails reside strictly on domestic Indian servers.
review_notes: Identified in LEG-INT-09; pending legal counsel verification.

title: Statutory Penalty Deficit Exposure and Sanction Audit
objective: Quantify potential statutory financial penalty exposure across statutory tiers and establish mitigating measures.
legal_reference_summary: The Schedule establishes five statutory financial penalty tiers up to ₹250 Crores based on breach nature, gravity, duration, repetitive nature, and mitigating measures taken.
applicability_conditions: Applies universally to all Data Fiduciaries and Processors.
assessment_question: Has the organisation assessed its potential statutory penalty exposure across the five statutory tiers and established mitigating measures recognized under Section 28(2)?
implementation_expectations: Conduct periodic statutory risk modeling quantifying potential penalty liabilities and documenting proactive mitigating measures.
evidence_limitations: Relying solely on cyber insurance without implementing technical mitigations does not satisfy DPBI mitigation criteria.
assessment_guidance: Check whether compliance deficits in Sections 8(5), 8(6), and 9 are tracked as enterprise board-level risks.
risk_guidance: Failure to remediate known statutory deficits constitutes a repetitive/aggravated factor under Section 28(2).
suggested_remediation: Present quarterly DPDP statutory deficit registers to executive leadership and prioritize funding for high-penalty risk gaps.
review_notes: Awaiting final TLI legal review under DEC-08.
